canonical_title: A Little Something for Us Tempunauts
author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Final Stage, edited by Edward L. Ferman and Barry N. Malzberg, 1974
card_summary: Three American time travelers — Addison Doug, Benz, and Crayne — return from history's first crewed time-travel launch only to learn, via television, that they were killed in an implosion on reentry.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A Clerk arrives to make sure a sleepy dog — the neighborhood's Summoner — barks at exactly 8:15 to bring insurance salesman Ed Fletcher 'A Friend with a Car,' getting him to his office an hour early before Sector T137 is taken offline for a scheduled 'adjustment.' The dog oversleeps by one minute.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Five years after a global war, a planet-wide network of automated factories continues to supply human settlements with food and goods, exactly as instructed before the collapse.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Planet Stories, July 1952 — the first Dick story to appear in print
card_summary: A ship provisioning on Mars takes aboard a wub — an enormous, placid, pig-like animal bought from a native for fifty cents by the crewman Peterson. Captain Franco intends to eat it; the ship's stores have spoiled and there is nothing to feed the crew for a month. The wub then speaks.

canonical_title: Chains of Air, Web of Aether
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Leo McVane lives alone in an isolated communications dome on a frozen, double-sunned world, his only real companionship the recorded voice of Linda Fox, a singer who reworks the Elizabethan lute songs of John Dowland for a scattered, exiled human diaspora.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A survey unit has spent three weeks on Planet Blue and found no harmful life form at all — no disease, no vermin, nothing. The place is so unspoiled that one officer has stopped smoking because he cannot bring himself to litter it, and the joke is that it might be Eden.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a sterile, uniform twenty-second century, George Miller curates the Twentieth Century exhibit at the History Agency, immersing himself so completely in his research period — its clothes, slang, briefcase, pipe tobacco — that his colleague Fleming warns him he is becoming a political liability.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, 1953
card_summary: An unnamed man crushes two eavesdropping caterpillars under his foot on his way to the bus, cautiously avoids a spider web, and rides home uneasy about an insect world he half-perceives is aware of him.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a Hanoi where the Party has won the global war, Tung Chien is a mid-level functionary at the Ministry of Cultural Artifacts. A legless war-veteran peddler compels him by law to buy a herbal remedy, and sells him what is described as something to rest eyes wearied by official monologues.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Jill Herrick is married to Lester, a toxicologist who develops poisons for the military and who treats warmth, metaphor, food and children as forms of imprecision.

canonical_title: I Hope I Shall Arrive Soon
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: On a ten-year interstellar crossing with sixty emigrants in cryonic suspension, one sleeper's tank malfunctions.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Spence Olham, a senior researcher on a wartime defense project against the alien Outspacers, is arrested on his morning commute by Major Peters of the security service and his own old friend Nelson, who tell him he is not human at all: an Outspace humanoid robot, containing a U-Bomb triggered by a spoken phrase, sent to kill and replace the real Olham and detonate once inside the Project.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a comfortable future household, a spherical robot Nanny raises the Fields children with total competence — waking them, walking them safely to school, disciplining them with iron patience, protecting them from bullies and drunks.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: After a nuclear war has reduced the world to ash and rubble, human settlements survive by trading their salvaged pre-war goods to the Biltong — alien, amoeba-like creatures drawn to Earth by the H-bomb flashes — who duplicate them.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: After six years reconstructing Mars following Terra's defeat in the Prox-Terra war, exhausted reconstruct engineer Milt Biskle asks to go home instead of accepting his reward — priority land on the world he rebuilt.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Peace officers stop John Cupertino for driving at 160 miles an hour, and find a man in quiet crisis: he insists that his surroundings are unreal, that he can pass his hand through solid objects, and that this all began with the death of his wife Carol — whom he remembers killing on Ganymede three years earlier.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Boris, a large black dog belonging to the Cardossi family, barks a single word — 'Roog' — at figures nobody else can see. The reader is given the dog's understanding from the first line and never leaves it.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Ed Morris commutes home from Ganymede to Earth through a solar system saturated with advertising — audio and visual ads that fire directly into commuters' brains, salesrobots that swarm pedestrians and cannot be shaken.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Six years into a nuclear war that has left most of the northern hemisphere ash, the American government has withdrawn to a Moon base and left its troops dug into bunkers on a dead Earth.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Verne Haskel, exhausted and embittered after twenty resentful years at Larson's Pump and Valve Works, retreats each evening to his basement, where he has spent his entire life building an obsessively exact miniature model of his hometown of Woodland — every store, house and street, down to the display cases in the shop windows.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Unpublished in his lifetime; held in the PKD Estate Archives
card_summary: In a future City of Lightness where citizens fly on mechanical wings, Robert Benton is summoned to the Controller's office and told that an invention he has no memory of submitting has been denied: humanity, having reached the absolute limit of its ingenuity a century earlier, adopted 'Stabilization' — a rigidly enforced freeze on all further change, backed by yearly exams, forced disappearances, and a fate called 'the Cart' for those who backslide.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Thirty years into a war that has stripped Earth's surface to ash and driven humanity into underground tunnels, a survey team leaps from a crashing rocket onto Mars, the last untested planet in the solar system, hoping to find a habitable refuge.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A tired commuter named Ernest Critchet asks ticket agent Ed Jacobson for a new commute book to a town called Macon Heights.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Overweight, food-obsessed schoolboy Bubber Surle visits an elderly, isolated widow, Mrs. Drew, purely for her fresh-baked cookies, tolerating her requests that he stay and read to her from his schoolbooks as the price of the treat.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Survivors of a hydrogen war — 'flukers', so named because they lived by a fluke of fate — shelter in underground pits, kept alive by Martian 'careboys' who parachute supplies they no longer need. The pits are full of food.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Eight years into a nuclear war, the entire human population of both blocs lives in sealed installations beneath the surface, manufacturing weapons that robots called leadies carry up and use.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, October 1969
card_summary: Garson Poole wakes in hospital after a crash, missing a right hand and feeling no pain, and is informed by his doctor that he is not a man but an 'electric ant' — an organic robot. The hospital cannot treat him, but bills him for services rendered up to the point of discovery.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Bob Bibleman, a floating-home salesman in a future where robots handle all low-wage work, idly answers a fast-food robot's contest question and wins, at two-trillion-to-one odds, a full scholarship to the College — an elite, unadvertised, military-chartered institution that selects rather than being selected.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Dark Side, edited by Damon Knight, 1976
card_summary: An aging Roman priest named Philos Diktos of Tyana ('Philip' transliterated into Greek and Latin) confesses, near the end of his life, a secret witnessed decades earlier at the temple of the Cumaean Sibyl, shortly after the assassination of Julius Caesar.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, December 1954
card_summary: Eight-year-old Charles Walton is sent to fetch his father for dinner and comes back unable to say which of them to fetch: there are two, and they look alike. The one that comes in to eat is the father-thing.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: If, April 1954 (Quinn Publishing Co.) — byline details confirmed by Dick himself in a 1975 letter to his agent
card_summary: In a post-war America where radiation has produced mutants — 'deeves' — the Department of Civic Anthropology hunts and euthanises them at birth; eighty-seven types have been catalogued and dealt with in sixty years.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Shadrach Jones, an old man running a nearly abandoned filling station in Derryville, Colorado, gives shelter one stormy night to a bedraggled party of Elves carrying their dying king on a platform.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Zen Buddhism scholar Joan Hiashi is recruited by the State Department to bring her expertise to Havana, ostensibly to convert wealthy Chinese-Cuban businessmen away from Communism, but really as bait: her lover, jazz harpist and telepath Ray Meritan, is suspected of connections to Mercerism, a new religious movement sweeping the world built around 'empathy boxes' — devices that let followers literally share, in real time, the suffering of Wilbur Mercer as he walks toward his death on an alien world.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: On Callisto, a team of anonymous 'yance-men' produce daily video 'gestalts' of John Edward Yancy, a folksy, avuncular composite personality — homespun wisdom, a devoted grandson, opinions on everything from primroses to just war — broadcast to the entire moon and treated by its population as the most beloved man alive.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, October 1974
card_summary: In a near-future California, Congress has extended abortion law past birth: a child has no soul, and so no legal protection, until it can do algebra — a test the law sets at twelve.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, June 1953
card_summary: Doc Labyrinth, convinced that civilisation is going the way of Rome and that a dark age is coming, worries that music is the most perishable of the things that will be lost.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Conger, a convicted smuggler and skilled hunter, is offered release from prison by a totalitarian Council in exchange for a mission: travel back in time to twentieth-century Colorado and kill the founder of the pacifist First Church before he ever preaches.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Centuries after an apocalyptic 'Time of Madness,' a rigid caste theocracy governs the survivors, its doctrine of reincarnation administered through a rusting, decaying 'scanner' technology that lets the faithful preview their next incarnation on the cosmic ladder.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a future where a crime is solved by a forensic 'file bank' that narrows the population from billions to a handful of suspects through successive physical specifications, an autonomous watchdog robot — an 'M' (machine), built to hunt poachers on frontier plantations — is diverted by wealthy slaver Paul Tirol to assassinate his own business front man, Heimie Rosenburg, and frame Tirol's business rival, David Lantano, by planting false forensic clues (blood type, hair, a heel print) engineered to point the investigation's ten specifications directly at Lantano.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Silvia, a young woman with an inherited gift for summoning vast, alien 'angels' by offering trays of lamb's blood in her family's garden, treats the ritual as a private thrill she has practiced since childhood — she believes herself descended from these beings and destined to eventually join them.

canonical_title: We Can Remember It For You Wholesale
author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, April 1966
card_summary: Douglas Quail, a clerk at the West Coast Emigration Bureau, wants to have gone to Mars and cannot afford to go.
